items.title: 台幣逼近32.5元還會貶？外銀看好強勁出口支撐 年底反攻31.5元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Near 32.5 per Dollar – Will It Depreciate Further? Foreign Banks See Strong Export Support, Expect a Rebound to 31.5 by Year‑End
paras: 分析師表示，全球市場對人工智慧（AI）交易的疑慮引發新台幣走弱，卻掩蓋了台灣經濟的基本韌性；穩健的經濟基本面可望支撐新台幣在年底前回升。
儘管新台幣近期承受沉重壓力，華僑銀行與荷蘭國際集團（ING）仍預期，新台幣將分別回升至兌1美元31.60元與31.50元，較目前水準升值約2%。
這些預測的依據，是台灣強勁的經濟成長與經常帳順差。儘管市場對AI股高估值的疑慮持續推動資金外流，短期壓抑匯率，分析師預期，未來幾個月貿易基本面的支撐終將占上風。
三菱日聯銀行（MUFG）亞洲全球市場研究主管Lin Li表示：「創紀錄的貿易順差與AI相關出口，持續為新台幣提供基本支撐。但外資證券投資流出、對外投資，以及美元與新台幣之間龐大的利差，目前正創造美元需求，抵銷這些支撐。」
她預期，新台幣年底前將升至兌1美元31.8元，並在2027年6月底進一步升至30.9元。
出口與順差強勁 外資撤出台股形成拉鋸
受全球先進晶片需求空前強勁帶動，台灣經常帳順差在2025年底達到近700億美元的歷史新高，近幾個月則溫和收窄。同時，政府將全年經濟成長率預測上修至逾10%，台灣可望迎來2010年以來首次雙位數成長。
不過，這些基本面優勢正與外資撤離潮相互拉鋸。外資周四賣超台股新台幣3,026億元（約93億美元），創單日新高，推動新台幣逼近今年以來兌1美元約32.50元的低點。
雖然分析師不認為這個價位是央行必須捍衛的防線，但仍密切關注，視其為央行可接受匯率區間的重要參考。
ING大中華區首席經濟學家宋林表示：「央行將試圖讓新台幣維持相對區間震盪。我不認為存在必須守住的明確防線，但今年以來，31.5至32.5元似乎一直是央行可以接受的區間。」
道富銀行亞太區總體策略師Jiuk Choi認為，央行更可能著重降低匯率波動，而非鎖定特定價位。他表示：「話雖如此，我們認為美元兌新台幣32.4至32.5元是重要區間，因為這是2026年以來的高點。」
油價與利差添壓力 中期仍看升
除了科技業疑慮，台灣作為能源進口國，偏高的原油價格也為新台幣增添壓力。此外，美國10年期公債殖利率較台灣同天期公債高出約300個基點，具吸引力的利差持續支撐美元普遍走強，壓抑區域貨幣表現。
LGT私人銀行外匯與利率專家Trang Le表示：「短期逆風包括外資撤出台股，以及聯準會立場偏鷹帶動美元走強。」
她指出：「即便如此，強勁的出口動能、穩健的對外收支，以及AI驅動的半導體景氣循環，仍使新台幣中期走勢偏向升值。我們預期，匯率波動將是主軸，而非持續走弱。」
科技財報成下一個匯率關鍵
匯市交易員正關注主要半導體製造商的財報，策略師視其為牽動跨境股市資金流向與匯率波動的下一個關鍵因素。台積電周四公布優於預期的營收展望，卻未能完全平息市場對整體AI基礎建設擴張的疑慮。
道富銀行的Choi表示：「接下來公布的全球科技業財報，可能加劇新台幣波動，尤其市場對AI相關資本支出、獲利能力及中國競爭的敏感度已升高。」
他認為，AI交易疑慮仍可能讓新台幣短期進一步走弱，但預期年底前將回升至兌1美元31.80元。
他表示：「我們認為，新台幣是對沖美元走強的最佳貨幣之一，因為資本與經常帳資金流仍然強勁，而且新台幣也是新興市場中波動率最低的貨幣之一。」
paras_en: Analysts say that global concerns over artificial‑intelligence (AI) trading have weakened the New Taiwan dollar, but this masks the underlying resilience of Taiwan’s economy; a solid economic foundation is expected to support a rebound of the currency before year‑end.

Even though the New Taiwan dollar has been under heavy pressure recently, both OCBC and ING forecast that it will recover to about NT$31.60 per US$1 and NT$31.50 per US$1 respectively, roughly a 2% appreciation from current levels.

These forecasts are based on Taiwan’s strong economic growth and current‑account surplus. Although market worries about over‑valued AI stocks continue to drive capital outflows and suppress the exchange rate in the short term, analysts expect the trade fundamentals to ultimately prevail in the coming months.

Lin Li, head of Asian Global Markets Research at MUFG, said: “Record‑high trade surpluses and AI‑related exports continuously provide fundamental support for the New Taiwan dollar. Yet foreign‑security outflows, outbound investment and the huge interest‑rate differential between the dollar and the New Taiwan dollar are currently creating dollar demand that offsets those supports.”
She projects the New Taiwan dollar will rise to NT$31.8 per US$1 by year‑end and further to NT$30.9 by the end of June 2027.
Strong exports and surplus, foreign‑capital pull‑out creates a tug‑of‑war in Taiwan equities

Fueled by unprecedented demand for advanced chips worldwide, Taiwan’s current‑account surplus is set to hit a historic high of nearly US$70 billion by the end of 2025, though it has narrowed modestly in recent months. At the same time, the government has lifted its full‑year growth forecast to above 10%, positioning Taiwan for its first double‑digit expansion since 2010.

However, these fundamental strengths are being contested by a wave of foreign‑capital outflows. On Thursday foreign investors sold NT$3,026 billion (about US$9.3 billion) of Taiwan equities, a single‑day record, pushing the New Taiwan dollar toward this year’s low of roughly NT$32.50 per US$1.
While analysts do not view this level as a hard floor the central bank must defend, they are watching it closely as an important reference for the exchange‑rate band the bank may tolerate.

Song Lin, chief economist for Greater China at ING, said: “The central bank will try to keep the New Taiwan dollar within a relative range. I don’t see a clear floor that must be defended, but since the start of the year the NT$31.5‑NT$32.5 band has seemed acceptable to the central bank.”

Jiuk Choi, global‑strategy head for Asia‑Pacific at State Street, believes the central bank is more likely to focus on reducing volatility rather than anchoring a specific level. He added: “That said, we see NT$32.4‑NT$32.5 per US$1 as a key zone because it marks the high point reached in 2026.”
Oil prices and interest‑rate spreads add pressure; medium‑term outlook still upward

Beyond tech‑sector concerns, Taiwan’s status as an energy‑importing nation means high crude‑oil prices add further pressure on the New Taiwan dollar. In addition, the U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield is about 300 basis points higher than Taiwan’s comparable bond, and the attractive spread continues to underpin a broadly strong dollar, suppressing regional currencies.
Trang Le, FX and rates specialist at LGT Private Bank, said: “Short‑term headwinds include foreign‑capital outflows from Taiwan equities and a hawkish Fed stance that is bolstering the dollar.”

She noted: “Even so, strong export momentum, solid external balances and an AI‑driven semiconductor cycle still tilt the medium‑term New Taiwan dollar trend toward appreciation. We expect exchange‑rate volatility to be the main driver, not a continued weakening.”
Tech earnings become the next exchange‑rate catalyst

FX traders are watching earnings reports from major semiconductor manufacturers, which strategists see as the next key factor influencing cross‑border equity flows and currency moves. TSMC’s Thursday earnings outlook beat expectations, but did not fully allay market concerns about the broader AI‑infrastructure expansion.

State Street’s Choi said: “The upcoming global tech earnings season could amplify New Taiwan dollar volatility, especially as market sensitivity to AI‑related capex, profitability and competition from China has risen.”
He believes AI‑trading worries could still push the New Taiwan dollar lower in the short term, but expects a rebound to NT$31.80 per US$1 by year‑end.

He added: “We see the New Taiwan dollar as one of the best hedges against a strong dollar because capital and current‑account flows remain robust, and the New Taiwan dollar is also among the least volatile currencies in emerging markets.”
